# OpenHabitTracker

> Free, open source app for taking notes, planning tasks, and tracking habits.
> No ads, no account, no subscription, and all data stays on your device.
> Native apps for Windows, Linux, macOS, iOS and Android, a web app, and optional self-hosted sync
> through a Docker image.

OpenHabitTracker measures a habit by how overdue it is rather than by an unbroken run of days.
Each habit has a repeat rule of count, interval and period, and the app shows the time elapsed since
the last completion as a percentage of that interval, so a 10-day habit 2 days overdue reads 120%
and a 4-day habit 2 days overdue reads 150%.
A streak counter exists but is not the main indicator: it is off by default, appears only inside a
habit's detail, and counts in the habit's own period, so a weekly habit has a streak of weeks.
Skipping a day raises the urgency percentage rather than erasing anything.

Two areas go deeper than this category usually does.

Search, filter and sort.
Six independently foldable sections: search, filter by date, by category, by priority, by status,
and sort.
Planned and done dates are filtered separately, each before, on, after or not on a date you pick.
A date filter takes either an absolute date or a relative day offset that is resolved against today
at query time, so a saved filter never goes stale.
The habit interval ratio is a filterable quantity rather than a badge, with a minimum and a maximum
bound, so "habits between 50 and 150 percent of their interval" is expressible.
There are 11 sort keys, chosen per content type.
Category and priority filters each render as check boxes, radio buttons or a drop-down.
Search covers note bodies and checklist items, not only titles, and highlights matches in place.
The done-date range can be inverted to show what was not completed in a window.

Customization.
25 settings on one screen, 26 themes plus dark mode, 20 languages, 12 item colours, 6 priority
levels.
Settings decide which page and which sidebar open at start, what each list row shows, which
calendars appear, how filters render, and how dense the lists are.
Six of them add or remove entire blocks from the habit detail, so the same habit is either a short
form or a full statistics page.
Settings persist, sync, and travel in the JSON and YAML exports.

Notes support Markdown, rendered inline in the list.
Tasks have a planned date and time, a duration, a checklist and a timer.
Habits have a repeat rule, a display metric of repetitions, time or quantity, a checklist, a timer,
a calendar and full completion history.
Categories group all three and carry a completion rule of all or any.
Import and export cover JSON, YAML, TSV and Markdown, plus import from a Google Keep Takeout ZIP.

## Site

- [Home](https://openhabittracker.net/): what the app does, screenshots, and downloads for every platform
- [Web app](https://pwa.openhabittracker.net): the full app in a browser, works offline, no account needed
- [Version history](https://openhabittracker.net/version-history.html): every release since 1.0.0, with downloads

## In detail

- [Customization](https://openhabittracker.net/customizable-habit-tracker.html): what can be turned on or off, per screen and per content type
- [Search, filter and sort](https://openhabittracker.net/habit-tracker-search-and-filter.html): the date filters, the overdue filter, and the filter that shows what was not done

## Comparisons with other habit trackers

- [Habit tracker comparison](https://openhabittracker.net/habit-tracker-comparison.html): against Habitica, Loop, Streaks and Everyday
- [Self-hosted habit tracker](https://openhabittracker.net/self-hosted-habit-tracker.html): against Beaver Habits, HabitTrove and HabitSync
- [Loop Habit Tracker alternative](https://openhabittracker.net/loop-habit-tracker-alternative.html): Loop for iPhone, desktop and the web
- [Google Keep alternative](https://openhabittracker.net/google-keep-alternative.html): with built-in Google Keep import
- [Habitica alternative](https://openhabittracker.net/habitica-alternative.html): without the RPG
- [Streaks alternative](https://openhabittracker.net/streaks-alternative.html): Streaks for Android, Windows and Linux
- [Everyday alternative](https://openhabittracker.net/everyday-alternative.html): unlimited free habits

## Source and self-hosting

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Jinjinov/OpenHabitTracker): GPL-3.0, written in C# and Blazor, one UI codebase running in six .NET hosts
- [Docker image](https://hub.docker.com/r/jinjinov/openhabittracker): single-user Blazor Server instance, amd64 and arm64, with JWT auth and a REST API
- [GitHub Container Registry](https://github.com/Jinjinov/OpenHabitTracker/pkgs/container/openhabittracker): the same image on ghcr.io

## Install

- [Microsoft Store](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9mwzmlxzzllr): Windows
- [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=net.openhabittracker): Android
- [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/openhabittracker/id6654885470?platform=iphone): iOS
- [Mac App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/openhabittracker/id6654885470?platform=mac): macOS
- [Flathub](https://flathub.org/apps/net.openhabittracker.OpenHabitTracker): Linux
- [Snap Store](https://snapcraft.io/openhabittracker): Linux
- [APKPure](https://apkpure.com/openhabittracker/net.openhabittracker): Android
- [GitHub releases](https://github.com/Jinjinov/OpenHabitTracker/releases): Android APK, auto-updating with Obtainium
